'''John Casey''' (12 May 1820, [[Kilbehenny]], [[County Limerick]], [[Ireland]] – 3 January 1891, [[Dublin]]) was a respected [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Geometry|geometer]]. He is most famous for [[Casey's theorem]] on a circle that is tangent to four other circles, an extension of [[Ptolemy's theorem]]. However, he contributed several novel proofs and perspectives on [[Euclidean geometry]]. He and [[Émile Lemoine]] are considered to be the co-founders of the modern geometry of the circle and the triangle.<ref>[https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/in-tribute-to-john-casey-founder-of-modern-geometry-1.4240914 In tribute to John Casey, founder of modern geometry] The Irish Times, May 12, 2020</ref>

==Biography==
He was born at Kilbehenny in Limerick, Ireland and educated locally at Mitchelstown, before becoming a teacher under the Board of National Education. He later became headmaster of the Central Model Schools in [[Kilkenny|Kilkenny City]]. He subsequently entered [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1858, where he was [[List of Scholars of Trinity College Dublin|elected a Scholar]] in 1861 and was awarded the degree of BA in 1862. He was then Mathematics Master at Kingston School (1862–1873), Professor of Higher Mathematics and Mathematical Physics at the newly founded [[Catholic University of Ireland]] (1873–1881) and Lecturer in Mathematics at its successor, the University College Dublin (1881–1891).<ref>[https://thatsmaths.com/2020/05/07/john-casey-a-founder-of-modern-geometry/ John Casey: a Founder of Modern Geometry] ThatsMaths, May 7, 2020 Irish Times</ref> 

==Honours and awards==
In 1869, the [[University of Dublin]] awarded Casey the Honorary Degree of Doctor of Laws. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in June 1875.<ref>{{MacTutor|title=John Casey|id=Casey}}</ref> He was elected to the [[Royal Irish Academy]] and in 1880 became a member of its council. In 1878 the Academy conferred upon him the much coveted Cunningham Gold Medal.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.mocavo.com/Proceedings-of-the-Royal-Irish-Academy-2/125174/142#141| title= Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy, 1878|accessdate = 10 December 2014}}</ref> His work was also acknowledged by the Norwegian Government, among others. He was elected a member of the Societe Mathematique de France in 1884 and received the honorary degree of Doctor of Laws from the [[Royal University of Ireland]] in 1885.

==Major works==
* 1880: [http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/012304305 ''On Cubic Transformations'']
* 1881: [https://archive.org/details/oncyclidessphero00case On Cyclides and Sphero-quartics], from [[Internet Archive]]
* 1882: [https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/21076 The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid], link from [[Project Gutenberg]]
* 1885: [https://archive.org/details/cu31924001520455 A Treatise on the Analytic Geometry of the Point, Line, Circle and Conic Sections], [https://archive.org/details/atreatiseonanal05casegoog Second edition, 1893], links from Internet Archive
* 1886 [https://archive.org/details/atreatiseonanal05casegoog A Sequel to the First Six Books of Euclid, 4th edition], link from Internet Archive
* 1886: ''A Treatise on Elementary Trigonometry'' (Dublin, 1886)
* 1888: [http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000360458 ''A Treatise on Plane Trigonometry containing an account of the Hyperbolic Functions'']
* 1889: [https://archive.org/details/atreatiseonsphe00casegoog ''A Treatise on Spherical Geometry''], link from Internet Archive
